laws.name: Coupled.step (with Coupled.left :2076)
laws.statement: def step (g₁ g₂ : V → V → V) (H₁ H₂ : V) (p : V × V) : V × V := (D.add (D.sub p.1 H₁) (g₁ (D.sub p.1 H₁) (D.sub p.2 H₂)), D.add (D.sub p.2 H₂) (g₂ (D.sub p.1 H₁) (D.sub p.2 H₂)))   -- D : Drawn V
laws.says: Two levels in any linearly ordered amounts with a cut-off subtraction. Each constant draw takes first, as much as there is. Each level's next value is what its draw leaves of it plus its own giving, a function of what the draws leave of both. Nothing is taken from one level and added to the other; what is drawn goes nowhere.

laws.name: Coupled.Ends / Coupled.Indexed.Ends / Coupled.Indexed.EndsUnder
laws.statement: def Ends (G : ι → (ι → V) → V) (H : ι → V) (part : (ι → V) → V) (s : ι → V) : Prop := ∃ N, ∀ k, part ((Law.run (step D G H) s).state (N + k)) = D.zero ;  def EndsUnder (f : (ι → Nat) → (ι → Nat)) (c : ι) (s : ι → Nat) : Prop := ∃ N, ∀ k, (Law.run f s).state (N + k) c = 0
laws.says: 'Ends' means: from some step on the level read off the state is nothing, at every later step. It is not 'reaches nothing once' and its negation is not 'always positive' or 'the draw is met'.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.step (with Indexed.left :2109, Below :2117, Rises :2120)
laws.statement: def step (G : ι → (ι → V) → V) (H : ι → V) (x : ι → V) : ι → V := fun i => D.add (D.sub (x i) (H i)) (G i (left D H x)) ;  def Below (x y : ι → V) : Prop := ∀ i, D.le (x i) (y i) ;  def Rises (g : (ι → V) → V) : Prop := ∀ e e', Below D e e' → D.le (g e) (g e')
laws.says: Any number of conditions indexed by any type, each under a constant draw, each giving to itself a function of what the draws leave of all. 'Mutual support' is the name for every giving being monotone in what is left of every condition, its own included.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.DependsOn, Downstream
laws.statement: def DependsOn (G : ι → (ι → V) → V) (i j : ι) : Prop := ∀ e : ι → V, e j = D.zero → G i e = D.zero ;  inductive Downstream G : ι → ι → Prop | refl (i) : Downstream G i i | dep {i j k} : DependsOn D G i j → Downstream G j k → Downstream G i k
laws.says: i depends on j where i gives nothing whenever nothing is left of j. Downstream is the chain of that. It is a property of what a giving reads; nothing passes along it.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.step_mono, run_below, ends_of_below
laws.statement: step_mono: (rises : ∀ i, Rises D (G i)) (H) (below : Below D x y) : Below D (step D G H x) (step D G H y).  ends_of_below: (rises : ∀ i, Rises D (G i)) (reads : ∀ x y, Below D x y → D.le (part x) (part y)) (below : Below D x y) (ends : Ends D G H part y) : Ends D G H part x
laws.says: In any amounts with a draw: under mutual support the step keeps the order of states condition by condition, so a level (read by an order-keeping part) that ends from a state ends from every state at or below it. One-way.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.drains
laws.statement: (depends : DependsOn D G i j) {x} (within : D.le (x j) (H j)) : step D G H x i = D.sub (x i) (H i)
laws.says: Any amounts. Where i depends on j and j's level is within j's draw, i's next level is what i's draw leaves of it.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.ends_after, ends_of_partner
laws.statement: ends_after (whole numbers): (depends : DependsOn Drawn.whole G i j) (within : ∀ k, state (N + k) j ≤ H j) : (∀ k, state (N + k) i = state N i - H i * k) ∧ (0 < H i → ∀ k, state (N + state N i + k) i = 0).  ends_of_partner: (depends : DependsOn Drawn.whole G i j) (pos : 0 < H i) (ends : Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w j) s) : Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w i) s
laws.says: Whole numbers. Where i depends on j and j stays within its draw from step N on, i falls by its draw every step; if i's draw is positive, i is nothing within as many further steps as its level. So wherever j ends and i's draw is positive, i ends. One-way. Proved by its own induction on k over `drains`.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.ends_downstream (with downstream_within :2201)
laws.statement: (pos : ∀ i j, DependsOn Drawn.whole G i j → 0 < H i) {s} : ∀ {i k}, Downstream Drawn.whole G i k → Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w k) s → Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w i) s
laws.says: The cascade of ends. Whole numbers; every condition that depends on any other has a positive draw. Then wherever a condition ends, every condition downstream of it through any chain of dependence ends. One-way.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.ends_together
laws.statement: (pos : ∀ i j, DependsOn Drawn.whole G i j → 0 < H i) {s} {i k} (there : Downstream Drawn.whole G i k) (back : Downstream Drawn.whole G k i) : Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w i) s ↔ Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w k) s
laws.says: Whole numbers, every dependent's draw positive: two conditions each downstream of the other end together or not at all. Two-way, but it ties one ending to another; it does not say where either happens.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.Chain.cascades
laws.statement: DependsOn Drawn.whole giving 2 1 ∧ DependsOn Drawn.whole giving 1 0 ∧ ¬ DependsOn Drawn.whole giving 2 0 ∧ Ends Drawn.whole giving (fun _ => 1) (fun w => w 0) start ∧ Ends Drawn.whole giving (fun _ => 1) (fun w => w 2) start
laws.says: One chain of three (index Nat; the first gives nothing, the second gives one where one is left of the first, the third one where one is left of the second; each starts at two; draws of one). The third does not depend on the first directly, the first ends, and the third ends.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.Chain.stopped
laws.statement: Ends Drawn.whole giving (fun i => if i = 1 then 0 else 1) (fun w => w 0) start ∧ Downstream Drawn.whole giving 2 0 ∧ ∀ n, (Law.run (step Drawn.whole giving fun i => if i = 1 then 0 else 1) start).state n 2 = 2
laws.says: The same chain with no draw on the second: the first still ends, the third is downstream of it, yet the third stays at two at every step. The positive-draw premise of the cascade cannot be dropped.

laws.name: Coupled.pair_run, ends_pair, pair_rises; Coupled.step_mono, run_below, ends_of_below; run_swap, ends_swap; Coupled.drains
laws.statement: pair_run: ∀ n, web run from (ofPair s) at true = (pair run from s at n).1 ∧ at false = (...).2, the web being Indexed.step D (pairGiving g₁ g₂) (pairDraw H₁ H₂).  ends_pair: Ends D g₁ g₂ H₁ H₂ part s ↔ Indexed.Ends D (pairGiving g₁ g₂) (pairDraw H₁ H₂) (fun w => part (w true, w false)) (ofPair s).  ends_swap: Ends D g₁ g₂ H₁ H₂ Prod.snd s ↔ Ends D (fun a b => g₂ b a) (fun a b => g₁ b a) H₂ H₁ Prod.fst s.swap.  Coupled.drains: (depends : ∀ b, g₂ D.zero b = D.zero) (within : D.le p.1 H₁) : (step D g₁ g₂ H₁ H₂ p).2 = D.sub p.2 H₂
laws.says: Any amounts. The pair is the web indexed by Bool, run for run; the pair's order and draining laws are the web's read for it; exchanging the two conditions exchanges the levels. The two iffs here are translations between two ways of writing the same run, not exactly-where laws.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.Band, Pointwise, ReadsPointwise
laws.statement: def Band (G : ι → (ι → Nat) → Nat) (H : ι → Nat) (hi : Nat) : Prop := ∀ x : ι → Nat, (∀ i, x i ≤ hi) → ∀ i, step Drawn.whole G H x i ≤ hi ;  def Pointwise G : Prop := ∀ i e e', (∀ j, e j = e' j) → G i e = G i e' ;  def ReadsPointwise (f : (ι → Nat) → (ι → Nat)) : Prop := ∀ x y, (∀ j, x j = y j) → ∀ i, f x i = f y i
laws.says: A band up to hi: the step keeps every state with all levels within hi within hi. Pointwise / ReadsPointwise: alike condition by condition gives alike (so no equality of functions is needed).

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.respects, pointwise_of_rises, step_alike, run_alike_of, pointwise_step, run_alike, ends_alike, run_shift
laws.statement: ends_alike: (pointwise : Pointwise G) (same : ∀ j, x j = y j) (i) : Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w i) x ↔ Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w i) y ; the rest are the pointwise congruences it rests on
laws.says: Whole numbers. Mutual support reads what is left condition by condition; states alike at every condition step, run and end alike. Bookkeeping laws.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.within_draw, left_falls, still_of_left (with given_within :2398, left_le :2405, run_within :2495)
laws.statement: within_draw: (rises : ∀ i, Rises Drawn.whole (G i)) (band : Band G H hi) (high : ∀ i, x i ≤ hi) (i) : G i (left Drawn.whole H x) ≤ H i.  left_falls: same premises on the start s, ∀ n i: state (n + 1) i - H i ≤ state n i - H i.  still_of_left: (rises) (same : ∀ j, state (n + 1) j - H j = state n j - H j) : ∀ k i, state (n + 1 + k) i = state (n + 1) i
laws.says: Whole numbers. Within a band under mutual support every condition gives at most its draw at every state in the band, so what the draws leave of each never rises along a run; and once a step leaves that alike at every condition the run is still. Inside a band nothing grows.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.rests_by, comes_to_rest
laws.statement: comes_to_rest: (rises : ∀ i, Rises Drawn.whole (G i)) (band : Band G H hi) {cs : List ι} (covers : ∀ i, i ∈ cs) (high : ∀ i, s i ≤ hi) : ∃ N, N ≤ cs.length * hi + 1 ∧ ∀ k i, state (N + k) i = state N i.  rests_by: the same with the bound d + 1 for any d with leftOver H s cs ≤ d
laws.says: Whole numbers, finitely many conditions (a list covering the index type), mutual support, a band, start within the band: the run is still, condition by condition, from some step at most (number listed) × hi + 1. Proved from Amounts.unmarked_within on the sum of what the draws leave.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.ends_iff
laws.statement: (rises : ∀ i, Rises Drawn.whole (G i)) (band : Band G H hi) (covers : ∀ i, i ∈ cs) (high : ∀ i, s i ≤ hi) (i : ι) : Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun x => x i) s ↔ (Law.run (step Drawn.whole G H) s).state (cs.length * hi + 1) i = 0
laws.says: Same premises: a condition ends exactly where it is nothing at step (count × hi + 1). Two-way; it says when the question is decided, not where in terms of givings.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.setAt, ending, threshold
laws.statement: def setAt (y : ι → Nat) (i : ι) (a : Nat) : ι → Nat := fun j => if j = i then a else y j ;  def ending G H K y i a : Bool := decide ((Law.run (step Drawn.whole G H) (setAt y i a)).state K i = 0) ;  def threshold G H cs hi y i : Nat := leading (ending G H (cs.length * hi + 1) y i) (hi + 1)
laws.says: Condition i's point of no return, the others as in y: the length of the leading run of levels 0, 1, ... (up to hi) from which i is nothing at step count × hi + 1. It is computed by running the step; it can be hi + 1 (every level in the band ends).

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.ends_iff_below (with ends_iff_ending :2678)
laws.statement: [DecidableEq ι] (rises : ∀ i, Rises Drawn.whole (G i)) {hi} (band : Band G H hi) {cs} (covers : ∀ i, i ∈ cs) {y} {i} {a} (high : a ≤ hi) (highs : ∀ j, y j ≤ hi) : Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun x => x i) (setAt y i a) ↔ a < threshold G H cs hi y i
laws.says: Whole numbers, finitely many conditions, mutual support, a band, the level a and all other levels within the band: condition i ends from level a exactly where a is below its threshold given the others. Two-way. Its content is that the ending levels are a down-set (from ends_of_below) cut exactly by the finite check (leading_exact, :1550).

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.threshold_falls
laws.statement: [DecidableEq ι] (rises) (band : Band G H hi) (covers) {y y'} {i} (le : ∀ j, y j ≤ y' j) (highs' : ∀ j, y' j ≤ hi) : threshold G H cs hi y' i ≤ threshold G H cs hi y i
laws.says: Same premises: raising any other level (within the band) does not raise i's threshold. One-way (not strict).

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.fates
laws.statement: [DecidableEq ι] (rises) (band) (covers) (high : a ≤ hi) (highs : ∀ j, y j ≤ hi) : ∃ N, N ≤ cs.length * hi + 1 ∧ (∀ k j, state (N + k) j = state N j) ∧ (a < threshold G H cs hi y i → state N i = 0) ∧ (threshold G H cs hi y i ≤ a → 0 < state N i)   -- states of the run from setAt y i a
laws.says: Same premises: the run is still from some bounded step; there condition i is nothing if it started below its threshold and something if not. This is the nearest thing in the part to 'goes on without end exactly where': one condition, given the others, rests at something for ever exactly from its (computed) threshold on.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.KeepsBelow, StaysWithin; step_keepsBelow, reads_of_keepsBelow, run_below_of, endsUnder_of_below, stays_at, within_below
laws.statement: def KeepsBelow (f : (ι → Nat) → (ι → Nat)) : Prop := ∀ x y, Below Drawn.whole x y → Below Drawn.whole (f x) (f y) ;  def StaysWithin f B s : Prop := ∀ n i, (Law.run f s).state n i ≤ B ;  step_keepsBelow: (rises : ∀ i, Rises Drawn.whole (G i)) : KeepsBelow (step Drawn.whole G H) ;  endsUnder_of_below: (keeps : KeepsBelow f) (below : Below Drawn.whole x y) (ends : EndsUnder f c y) : EndsUnder f c x ;  within_below: (keeps) (below x y) (within : StaysWithin f B y) : StaysWithin f B x
laws.says: For any law f of whole-number states: keeping the order implies reading condition by condition; ending and staying within a bound pass down the order. The web's step keeps the order under mutual support.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.returns_within, repeats (with levels, levelLists, levelLists_length :2750-2810)
laws.statement: returns_within: (covers : ∀ i, i ∈ cs) (within : StaysWithin f B s) : ∃ i j, i < j ∧ j ≤ (B + 1) ^ cs.length ∧ ∀ c, (Law.run f s).state i c = (Law.run f s).state j c.  repeats: (reads : ReadsPointwise f) (same : ∀ c, state i c = state j c) : ∀ m c, state (i + m) c = state (j + m) c
laws.says: Any law f, finitely many conditions: a run that stays within B comes back, within (B+1)^count steps, to a state it was in (pigeonhole), and if f reads condition by condition it repeats from there. returns_within needs no premise on f at all.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.ends_iff_within (with repeats_mul :2883, zero_from_window :2892)
laws.statement: (reads : ReadsPointwise f) (covers : ∀ i, i ∈ cs) (within : StaysWithin f B s) (c : ι) : (EndsUnder f c s ↔ ∀ m, m ≤ (B + 1) ^ cs.length → (Law.run f s).state ((B + 1) ^ cs.length + m) c = 0) ∧ (EndsUnder f c s → ∀ k, (Law.run f s).state ((B + 1) ^ cs.length + k) c = 0)
laws.says: Any law reading condition by condition, finitely many conditions, a run within B: a condition ends exactly where it is nothing at every step from L to 2L, L = (B+1)^count, and then it is nothing from L on. No band, no order, no mutual support. Two-way; a decision procedure, not a where.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.endingWithin, thresholdWithin
laws.statement: def endingWithin f L y i a : Bool := below (fun m => decide ((Law.run f (setAt y i a)).state (L + m) i = 0)) (L + 1) ;  def thresholdWithin f cs B hi y i : Nat := leading (endingWithin f ((B + 1) ^ cs.length) y i) (hi + 1)
laws.says: The point of no return beyond a band, again computed by running the law (over the window L to 2L).

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.ends_iff_below_within (with ending_iff :2972)
laws.statement: [DecidableEq ι] {f} (keeps : KeepsBelow f) {cs} (covers : ∀ i, i ∈ cs) {B hi} {y} {i} {a} (within : StaysWithin f B (setAt y i hi)) (high : a ≤ hi) : EndsUnder f i (setAt y i a) ↔ a < thresholdWithin f cs B hi y i
laws.says: Any order-keeping law of whole-number states, finitely many conditions, where the run from i at the top level hi (others as in y) stays within B: i ends from a ≤ hi exactly where a is below the computed threshold. laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.Recent.step, Recent.Rises
laws.statement: def step (G : ι → (ι → Nat) → (ι → Nat) → Nat) (H : ι → Nat) (x : ι × Bool → Nat) : ι × Bool → Nat | (i, true) => (x (i, true) - H i) + G i (fun j => x (j, true) - H j) (fun j => x (j, false)) | (i, false) => G i (fun j => x (j, true) - H j) (fun j => x (j, false)) ;  def Rises G : Prop := ∀ i e e' r r', (∀ j, e j ≤ e' j) → (∀ j, r j ≤ r' j) → G i e r ≤ G i e' r'
laws.says: Whole numbers only. The state holds, for each condition, its level and what it gave at the last step; its giving is a function of what the draws leave of all and of what each gave last; what it gives now is its next 'recent giving'. Draws constant; giving again goes to the giver's own level.

laws.name: Coupled.Indexed.Recent.keepsBelow, plain, adjusted (with both, mem_both, covers_both)
laws.statement: keepsBelow: (rises : Rises G) : KeepsBelow (step G H).  plain: (pointwise : Indexed.Pointwise G') (x) : ∀ n i, (Law.run (step (fun i e _ => G' i e) H) x).state n (i, true) = (Law.run (Indexed.step Drawn.whole G' H) (fun j => x (j, true))).state n i.  adjusted: (A : Nat → Nat → Nat) (H) (p) : ∀ n, [run of step (fun _ e r => A (e ()) (r ())) (fun _ => H) from ofAdjusted p] at ((), true) = ((Law.run (Adjusted.step A H) p).state n).1 ∧ at ((), false) = (...).2

Its rest, ending and thresholds are not stated separately: they follow only by putting Recent.step for f in ends_iff_within, ends_iff_below_within and threshold_falls_within, with ι × Bool as the index, so the bound B must also bound the recent givings.

laws.says: One built pair in whole numbers under draws of one. Both givings rise; each gives nothing where nothing is left of the other; the first ends from every level when the second starts at nothing, and the second likewise; from the one start (2, 3) the run alternates (2, 3), (3, 2) for ever, so both levels stay within three, neither ends, and the run is never still. All three steps (pair :2081, web :2113, with recent giving :3024) have the same shape: next level of i = (level of i less its constant draw, cut off at nothing) + G i (what the draws leave of all [, what each gave last]). So: (a) draws are constants of the step, the same at every step and every state, and what is drawn goes nowhere; (b) a condition's giving goes to its own level and comes from nowhere; (c) nothing passes from one condition to another, and no condition loses what another gains; another's level is only read; (d) there are no units, no takers, nothing that multiplies or is selected. The pair and web steps are in any `Drawn` amounts; rest, cascade and thresholds are in whole numbers; the step with recent giving is whole numbers only.

Inside a band, mutual support means running down. `within_draw` (:2489) proves that under mutual support and a band every condition gives at most its draw at every state of the band, hence `left_falls` (:2501). So every in-band law (rest, exact threshold, fates) is a law of levels that fall or stand. Growth appears only beyond a band. laws.name: Web.roles, Flow.roles and the embedding iffs
laws.where: Roles.lean:189 (Web.roles), :302 (Flow.roles), :217 roles_dependent, :223 roles_renewed, :235 roles_consumed, :240 roles_renewingIn, :246 roles_consumingIn, :251 roles_undermining, :258 roles_arises, :269 roles_unceasing, :327 roles_balances, :346 roles_more, :354 roles_acting, :362 roles_taking, :375 roles_dissipative
laws.statement: def roles (W : Web F C) : Web (F ⊕ C) (F ⊕ C); e.g. `W.roles.Dependent ↔ W.Dependent`, `L.roles.Balances W.roles ↔ L.Balances W`, `L.roles.Dissipative ↔ L.Dissipative`
laws.says: A two-kind web or flow read as one kind (formations at level 0, conditions never active) keeps each listed property exactly. No premise beyond the definitions.

laws.name: Web.roles_not_embodied / roles_not_selfBearing
laws.statement: (active : W.active t f) : ¬ W.roles.Embodied (.inl f); (active : W.active t f) : ¬ W.roles.SelfBearing (.inl f)
laws.says: In the embedded two-kind reading, a formation active at some step is never embodied and never bears on itself.

laws.name: Web.Embodied, Web.SelfBearing
laws.statement: def Embodied (x : X) : Prop := ∀ t, W.active t x ↔ 0 < W.level t x; def SelfBearing (x : X) : Prop := ∀ t, W.active t x → W.requires t x x ∧ 0 < W.need t x x  (W : Web X X)
laws.says: Embodied: active exactly while its own level is positive. Bears on itself: while active it requires its own level at a positive need.

laws.name: SelfBearing.stands; SelfBearing.met_iff
laws.statement: stands (dependent : W.Dependent) (self : W.SelfBearing x) (active : W.active t x) : 0 < W.level t x; met_iff (dependent) (embodied : W.Embodied x) (self) (t) : (W.requires t x x ∧ 0 < W.need t x x ∧ W.need t x x ≤ W.level t x) ↔ W.active t x
laws.says: Under Dependent, a self-bearing relatum stands while active; if also embodied its self-dependence is met exactly while it is active (it records nothing beyond the activity).

laws.name: Embodied.active_of_bearing
laws.statement: (dependent : W.Dependent) (embodied : W.Embodied y) (active : W.active t g) (bearing : W.requires t g y ∧ 0 < W.need t g y) : W.active t y
laws.says: Under Dependent, a formation active at t that requires an embodied relatum at a positive need: that relatum is active at t. One way; nothing about taking.

laws.name: Web.active_along, Web.coextinct (NOT in Roles.lean)
laws.statement: def bearing (t) : Process X Unit := ⟨fun g _ y => (W.requires t g y ∧ 0 < W.need t g y) ∧ W.Embodied y⟩; active_along (dependent : W.Dependent) (t) : Invariant (W.bearing t) (W.active t); coextinct (dependent) (chain : Reach (W.bearing t) g y) (ended : ¬ W.active t y) : ¬ W.active t g
laws.says: Under Dependent, at one step, along any chain of positive-need requirements on embodied relata: if the end is not active, the start is not active. An ending law at a single step; I did not read `Invariant`/`Reach`.

laws.name: Embodied.ends_when_consumed
laws.statement: (embodied : W.Embodied y) (least : W.need T g y ≤ 1) (below : ∀ t, T < t → W.level t y < W.need T g y) : ∀ t, T < t → ¬ W.active t y
laws.says: If after T the level of an embodied y stays below a need of at most one, y is not active after T. (`requires` is not a premise.)

laws.name: Embodied.ending_breaks
laws.statement: (dependent : W.Dependent) (embodied : W.Embodied x) (self : W.SelfBearing x) (active : W.active t x) (ends : ¬ W.active (t + 1) x) (drawn : W.draws t f x) : W.BreakingOn t f x
laws.says: Any formation drawing on an embodied, self-bearing relatum across the step at which it ends is breaking on it, whatever ends it (co-occurrence, not causation).

laws.name: Web.Dependent.inactive_below / ceases_below (and _at forms)
laws.statement: ceases_below (dependent : W.Dependent) (active : W.active t g) (below : W.level (t + 1) c < W.need t g c) (persists : W.requires (t + 1) g c) (noLess : W.need t g c ≤ W.need (t + 1) g c) : W.Ceases t g  (W : Web F C)
laws.says: Under Dependent, a requirement left below its need across a step, persisting at no lower need, belongs to a formation not active after the step; if it was active, it ceases.

laws.name: Embodied.arises_given
laws.statement: {L : Flow X X} (balances : L.Balances W) (acting : L.Acting W) (embodied : W.Embodied x) (arises : W.Arises t x) : ∃ f, W.active t f ∧ f ∈ L.present t ∧ 0 < L.give t f x ∧ f ≠ x
laws.says: In a balanced flow where only active formations give, an embodied relatum that arises is given to by an active formation taking part, other than itself. Nothing is said of what that giver takes or requires.

laws.name: Embodied.arises_from_embodied
laws.statement: (balances) (acting) (gives_embodied : ∀ t f c, f ∈ L.present t → 0 < L.give t f c → W.Embodied f) (embodied : W.Embodied x) (arises : W.Arises t x) : ∃ f, W.Embodied f ∧ 0 < W.level t f ∧ f ∈ L.present t ∧ 0 < L.give t f x ∧ f ≠ x
laws.says: If in addition every giver is embodied (a supplied premise), the giver stands as a condition while it gives.

laws.name: Web.relabel; relabel_dependent, relabel_undermining, relabel_alive
laws.statement: relabel_dependent (onto : ∀ c, ∃ y, π y = c) : (W.relabel π).Dependent ↔ W.Dependent; relabel_undermining (onto) (t) (f) : (W.relabel π).UnderminingAt t f ↔ W.UnderminingAt t f
laws.says: Relabelling which condition is which relatum, by a map onto the conditions, keeps Dependent and undermining. (It does not keep Embodied or SelfBearing: built examples :806, :960.)

laws.name: Embodied.comesToStand; given_of_arises; replenishes; embodiedArising_needs_replenishment
laws.statement: comesToStand (embodied : W.Embodied x) (arises : W.Arises t x) : W.ComesToStand t x; given_of_arises (balances : L.Balances W) (embodied) (arises) : W.level (t + 1) x ≤ L.given t x; replenishes (balances) (embodied) (mem : x ∈ cs) (arises) : 0 < L.replenishment cs t; embodiedArising_needs_replenishment (balances) (arising : ∀ N, ∃ t x, N ≤ t ∧ x ∈ cs ∧ W.Embodied x ∧ W.Arises t x) (T) : ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.replenishment cs t = 0
laws.says: An embodied arising is a level rising from zero; under balance it is given at least the level it arises with, so it is a giving to every family containing it; arising at arbitrarily late steps means giving to the family recurs.

laws.name: Embodied.arising_lowers_on (and arising_lowers_at, arising_lowers)
laws.statement: (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipates : L.DissipatesOn ds t) (embodied : W.Embodied x) (mem : x ∈ ds) (arises : W.Arises t x) : W.stock ds (t + 1) < W.stock ds t
laws.says: Balanced, and with every formation present giving the family ds strictly less than it takes from it when it takes (DissipatesOn), the arising of an embodied member of ds lowers the total level of ds. `arising_lowers` gets DissipatesOn from Dissipative + Distinct ds + ClosedAt ds t.

laws.name: Embodied.arising_with_fall
laws.statement: (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipates : L.DissipatesOn ds t) (embodied : W.Embodied x) (mem : x ∈ ds) (arises : W.Arises t x) : ∃ y, y ∈ ds ∧ y ≠ x ∧ W.Falls t y
laws.says: Under the same premises another member of the family falls across the same step. Which member, and whether anything requires it, is not said.

laws.name: embodiedArising_not_recurring_on / _from
laws.statement: (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipates : ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.DissipatesOn ds t) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t x, N ≤ t ∧ x ∈ ds ∧ W.Embodied x ∧ W.Arises t x
laws.says: In a family dissipated on from some step on, embodied members do not arise at arbitrarily late steps.

laws.name: embodiedArising_opens
laws.statement: (balances) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) (distinct : Distinct ds) (arising : ∀ N, ∃ t x, N ≤ t ∧ x ∈ ds ∧ W.Embodied x ∧ W.Arises t x) (T) : ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.ClosedAt ds t
laws.says: Under balance and dissipation, a finite family in which embodied members keep arising is not closed from any step on. The exchange that opens it need not touch the family (SprayShuttle).

laws.name: embodiedArising_draws_in / _from
laws.statement: (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) (distinct : Distinct ds) (around : ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → L.Around ds t) (arising : ∀ N, ∃ t x, N ≤ t ∧ x ∈ ds ∧ W.Embodied x ∧ W.Arises t x) (N) : ¬ ∀ t, N ≤ t → L.Inward ds t
laws.says: If also from T₀ on each step is closed within some finite family containing ds, then it is not the case that from N on every giver to ds takes only from ds: at arbitrarily late steps (stated as a negation) something that gives to ds takes from beyond it.

laws.name: embodiedArising_not_recurring
laws.statement: (balances) (dissipative) (distinct : Distinct all) (every : ∀ x, x ∈ all) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t x, N ≤ t ∧ W.Embodied x ∧ W.Arises t x
laws.says: If finitely many relata are all there is, under balance and dissipation embodied relata do not arise at arbitrarily late steps.

laws.name: Mutualism (web, apart, renewing, alive, apart_relabelled)
laws.statement: web: level _ _ := 1, active _ _ := True, requires _ _ _ := True, need := 1, draws _ x y := y = other x. renewing (x) : web.RenewingIn x; alive (e) : web.active e.2 e.1 ∧ ¬ web.UnderminingAt e.2 e.1; apart_relabelled : (∀ x, ¬ apart.SelfBearing x) ∧ (∀ x, (apart.relabel other).SelfBearing x) ∧ ((apart.relabel other).Dependent ↔ apart.Dependent)
laws.says: Two relata each requiring itself and the other at need 1 and drawing on the other; all levels are 1 and all activity True by definition. There is no flow in the module (Space.lean:378 pairs it with Flow.still): nothing is taken or given, and nothing arises. 'Renew each other' is constant levels.

laws.name: Predation (web, hare_ends, breaking); fox_ends
laws.statement: web: level t _ := uneaten t; active t _ := 0 < uneaten t; requires _ x y := y = x ∨ y = .hare; draws _ x y := x = .fox ∧ y = .hare. breaking : web.BreakingOn 2 .fox .hare; fox_ends : ∀ t, 2 < t → ¬ web.active t .fox
laws.says: Fox and hare share one stipulated schedule (1,1,1,0,...). The fox's draw at step 2 is breaking by ending_breaks; the fox's ending follows from coextinct and also holds by the definition of the web. No flow.

laws.name: Wilting.wilting; Wilting.relabelled_not_embodied
laws.statement: flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Taking web ∧ web.Dependent ∧ web.Embodied .flower ∧ web.SelfBearing .flower ∧ (∀ t c, flow.take t .bee c = 0) ∧ (∀ t f, 0 < flow.take t f .flower → f = .flower) ∧ web.BreakingOn 2 .bee .flower ∧ web.UnderminingAt 2 .bee ∧ web.UnderminingAt 2 .flower
laws.says: A flower takes one unit from itself at step 2 and ends; a bee draws on it and takes nothing, ever; the bee's event at step 2 is still undermining. Relabelled by swap, the flower is not embodied.

laws.name: Brood.brood; not_dissipative; rise_without_fall
laws.statement: brood : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ web.Dependent ∧ (∀ x, web.Embodied x ∧ web.SelfBearing x) ∧ web.Unceasing; not_dissipative : ¬ flow.Dissipative; rise_without_fall (t) : flow.ClosedAt [t, t + 1] t ∧ web.Arises t (t + 1) ∧ (∀ s x, ¬ web.Falls s x) ∧ ¬ flow.DissipatesOn [t, t + 1] t
laws.says: Generation t gives one unit to generation t+1 at step t and takes nothing (take := 0); each generation requires only itself. Arising never ceases and no level ever falls. The giving is from nothing: the flow is proved not dissipative.

laws.name: SourceSeed.source_gives
laws.statement: flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ web.Embodied .seed ∧ web.Arises 0 .seed ∧ (∀ f, web.active 0 f ∧ f ∈ flow.present 0 ∧ 0 < flow.give 0 f .seed ∧ f ≠ .seed → f = .source) ∧ ¬ web.Embodied .source ∧ ¬ web.SelfBearing .source ∧ ∀ t c, ¬ web.requires t .source c
laws.says: The giver named by arises_given need not be embodied, bear on itself or require anything: a source at level 0, always active, gives the seed one unit and takes nothing.

laws.name: EmbodiedSource.embodied_source
laws.statement: SourceSeed.flow.Balances web ∧ SourceSeed.flow.Acting web ∧ (∀ t f c, f ∈ present t → 0 < give t f c → web.Embodied f) ∧ web.Embodied .seed ∧ web.Arises 0 .seed ∧ (∃ f, web.Embodied f ∧ 0 < web.level 0 f ∧ f ∈ present 0 ∧ 0 < give 0 f .seed ∧ f ≠ .seed) ∧ (∀ t c, ¬ web.requires t .source c ∧ ¬ web.draws t .source c ∧ SourceSeed.flow.take t .source c = 0) ∧ ¬ web.SelfBearing .source
laws.says: The same flow with the source standing at 1: every premise of arises_from_embodied holds and the embodied giver it names requires, draws on and takes nothing. Being embodied is a reading of standing.

laws.name: Shuttle.shuttle (with next_off)
laws.statement: flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ web.Dependent ∧ (∀ x, web.Embodied x ∧ web.SelfBearing x) ∧ (∀ t, flow.ClosedAt [true, false] t) ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ ¬ flow.Dissipative; next_off : ∀ t, stands (holder t) (t + 1) = 0
laws.says: Two sides hand one unit back and forth: the holder takes its own unit (which it requires at need 1) and gives it to the other, which arises as the holder falls to nothing. Closed, two relata, arising unceasing; only dissipation fails.

laws.name: Throughput.throughput; frontier; draws_in
laws.statement: throughput : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ web.Dependent ∧ (∀ x, web.Embodied (.side x) ∧ web.SelfBearing (.side x)) ∧ flow.Dissipative ∧ ∀ x N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ web.Arises t (.side x); draws_in (N) : ¬ ∀ t, N ≤ t → flow.Inward [.side true, .side false] t
laws.says: Shuttle with the holder also burning two units of a fresh fuel each step: dissipative, arising recurs, every finite family containing a side is open at arbitrarily late steps, and the sides draw in the fuel. The fuel is required by nothing and never active.

laws.name: SprayShuttle.spray_shuttle; opens_anyway
laws.statement: flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ web.Dependent ∧ (∀ x, web.Embodied (.side x) ∧ web.SelfBearing (.side x)) ∧ flow.Dissipative ∧ (∀ t, ¬ flow.Enclosed t) ∧ (∀ x N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ web.Arises t (.side x)) ∧ (∀ t, flow.Inward sides t) ∧ (∀ t x, flow.take t .sink (.side x) = 0 ∧ flow.give t .sink (.side x) = 0) ∧ ∀ t, web.stock sides t = 1
laws.says: With an unrelated sink exchanging with unboundedly many relata, no step is enclosed, so Dissipative holds vacuously; arising recurs in the two sides with nothing flowing in and their stock constant at 1.

laws.name: Flicker.flicker
laws.statement: flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Dissipative ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ ¬ web.Embodied ()
laws.says: One relatum, never standing, active at odd steps, empty flow: arising recurs under balance and dissipation in a world of one relatum. Only embodiment fails.

laws.name: Successive.relay
laws.statement: flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Dissipative ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ (∀ t, flow.takers [.pool] t = 1) ∧ (∀ t, flow.FedFromBeyond [.pool] t) ∧ (∀ m t t', Formation.source m ∈ flow.present t → Formation.source m ∈ flow.present t' → t = t') ∧ ∀ m t t', web.active t (.source m) → web.active t' (.source m) → t = t'
laws.says: The only result of the module. One source per step, active at its own step by definition, burns two units of that step's fuel and gives the pool one; an eater, always active by definition, takes one from the pool each step. Two-kind web (Formation, Condition), `requires` False everywhere, pool level 0 at every step. It has levels and takes; no source's arising is derived.

laws.name: Web.revisits_of_bounded; revisits_of_nonrising; returns_of_bounded
laws.statement: revisits_of_bounded (bound : ∀ t, T ≤ t → W.stock cs t ≤ K) (M) : ∃ i j, M ≤ i ∧ i < j ∧ W.config cs (T + i) = W.config cs (T + j); returns_of_bounded (bound) (changing : ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ W.Changes cs t) : ¬¬ W.Revisits cs T
laws.says: On any web, no flow: a fixed finite family of conditions whose total level stays within K from T on takes the same list of levels at two steps, from every step on.

laws.name: Web.exceeds_of_distinct_configs; unbounded_of_distinct_configs; exceeds_of_new; unbounded_of_new; unbounded_of_never_revisits
laws.statement: unbounded_of_new (new : ∀ i j, i < j → W.config cs (T + i) ≠ W.config cs (T + j)) (K M) : ∃ t, M ≤ t ∧ K < W.stock cs t
laws.says: A fixed finite family whose list of levels is different at every step from T on has total level above every bound at arbitrarily late steps. 'New' is a new list of levels of the same conditions, not a new formation; formations, activity and taking do not occur.

laws.name: Web.unread_of_new_record; unread_of_unbounded; Flow.uncarried_of_bounded; World.forgets_of_bounded
laws.statement: uncarried_of_bounded (bound : ∀ t, T ≤ t → W.stock cs t ≤ K) (exchanging : ∀ M, ∃ t, M ≤ t ∧ 0 < L.exchanges cs t) : ¬ L.CarriesHistory W cs T
laws.says: A family held within a bound cannot carry, in its levels, a record that never repeats or a count of its exchanges.

laws.name: Web.never_revisits_of_loses; changes_le_stock; rests_of_loses
laws.statement: rests_of_loses (still : ∀ t, T ≤ t → W.stock cs (t + 1) ≤ W.stock cs t) (loses : ∀ t, T ≤ t → W.Changes cs t → W.stock cs (t + 1) < W.stock cs t) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ W.Changes cs t
laws.says: A family whose total never rises and falls at every change changes at most as many times as its total at T; change does not recur.

laws.name: Web.counting, counting_new, counting_gains
laws.statement: def counting : Web Unit Unit := ⟨fun t _ => t, fun _ _ => False, ...⟩; counting_gains (K M) : ∃ t, M ≤ t ∧ K < counting.stock [()] t
laws.says: One condition whose level is the step, nothing active, no flow: new at every step.

laws.name: Flow.Balances.bounded; Flow.bounded_counting_rest; first_law_cases
laws.statement: Balances.bounded (balances : L.Balances W) (gainless : ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.GainlessOn cs t) : ∀ t, T ≤ t → W.stock cs t ≤ W.stock cs T
laws.says: The only places taking enters Novelty: a balanced family gaining nothing stays within its total at T, so the earlier Entropy forms are cases.

laws.name: Flow.AroundStanding; Flow.ExchangeRecurs
laws.statement: def AroundStanding (L) (stand : Nat → List C) (t) : Prop := ∃ es, Distinct es ∧ (∀ c, c ∈ stand t → c ∈ es) ∧ (∀ c, c ∈ stand (t + 1) → c ∈ es) ∧ L.ClosedAt es t; def ExchangeRecurs (L) : Prop := ∀ N, ∃ t f c, N ≤ t ∧ f ∈ L.present t ∧ (0 < L.take t f c ∨ 0 < L.give t f c)
laws.says: A step is enclosed around what stands when one finite closed family holds everything with a positive level before or after it.

laws.name: Flow.standing_runs_down; standing_never_rises; change_lowers; exchange_lowers
laws.statement: exchange_lowers (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) (census : W.StandingCensus stand) (around : L.AroundStanding stand t) (present : f ∈ L.present t) (exchanges : 0 < L.take t f c ∨ 0 < L.give t f c) : W.stock (stand (t + 1)) (t + 1) < W.stock (stand t) t
laws.says: Under balance, dissipation, a listing of what stands, and enclosure of the step around it: total standing does not rise, and any rise or fall of a level, or any take or give at all, lowers it.

laws.name: Flow.change_not_recurring_from; change_stops_unrefuted(_around); exchange_not_recurring_from/_around; World.exchange_not_recurring
laws.statement: exchange_not_recurring_around (balances) (dissipative) (census : W.StandingCensus stand) (around : ∀ t, T ≤ t → ¬¬ L.AroundStanding stand t) : ¬ L.ExchangeRecurs
laws.says: Where every step from some step on is (not refuted to be) enclosed around what stands, no formation takes or gives at arbitrarily late steps, and change of levels does not recur. No census of activity and no embodiment needed.

laws.name: Web.StandingCensus.coming_of_ceasing; coming_iff_ceasing; over_stretch
laws.statement: coming_iff_ceasing (census : W.StandingCensus stand) (bounded : ∀ t, T ≤ t → (stand t).length ≤ B) : (∀ N, ∃ t c, N ≤ t ∧ W.ComesToStand t c) ↔ ∀ N, ∃ t c, N ≤ t ∧ W.CeasesToStand t c
laws.says: With what stands listed and at most B standing from T on, conditions come to stand at arbitrarily late steps exactly when conditions cease to stand at arbitrarily late steps. A counting law; no flow.

laws.name: World.arising_of_ceasing; CountedWithin.arising_iff_ceasing; CountedBy.arising_iff_ceasing
laws.statement: CountedWithin.arising_iff_ceasing [∀ t x, Decidable (w.web.active t x)] (counted : w.CountedWithin B) : w.ArisingRecurs ↔ w.CeasingRecurs; CountedBy.arising_iff_ceasing (counted : w.CountedBy B) (returns : ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ B t ≤ K) : w.ArisingRecurs ↔ w.CeasingRecurs
laws.says: With decided activity and at most B relata active at each step (or a bound that returns to at most K at arbitrarily late steps), arising recurs exactly when ceasing recurs. Counts of the active only; levels and taking do not occur.

laws.name: World.census_one_way; accretion_unbounded; procession_world; slow_world
laws.statement: slow_world (grows : ∀ t, B t ≤ B (t + 1)) (unbounded : ∀ n, ∃ t, n < B t) : (slow B).CountedBy B ∧ (slow B).ArisingRecurs ∧ ∀ t x, ¬ (slow B).web.Ceases t x
laws.says: Built worlds (all with Flow.still and levels 0, or defined in Space): arising without end with nothing ceasing where the count is unbounded (accretion; slow B for every non-decreasing unbounded B); one relatum active at a time with both recurring (procession).

laws.name: World.arising_not_recurring_from; arising_stops_unrefuted(_from); comes_to_rest_unrefuted(_from); rests_unrefuted_around; rest_few
laws.statement: comes_to_rest_unrefuted (counted : w.Counted) (standing : w.web.StandingCensus stand) (embodied : w.ArisingEmbodied) (balanced : w.Balanced) (dissipative : w.Dissipative) (around : ∀ t, T ≤ t → w.flow.AroundStanding stand t) : ¬ ¬ ∃ N, w.RestsFrom N
laws.says: The rest theorem: with a census of what is active and of what stands, whatever arises embodied, balance, dissipation, and every step from T on enclosed around what stands, that the world rests from some step on cannot be refuted. Concludes ¬¬∃, not a named step.

laws.name: World.arising_opens
laws.statement: (counted : w.Counted) (embodied : w.Embodied) (balanced : w.Balanced) (dissipative : w.Dissipative) (arising : w.ArisingRecurs) (T : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → w.flow.Enclosed t
laws.says: With a census, every relatum embodied, balance and dissipation, arising without end is incompatible with every step from some step on being enclosed.

laws.name: Listed.few_of_quiet; few_of_stop_unrefuted; lpo_of_few
laws.statement: few_of_quiet (listed : Listed p l) (quiet : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t a, N ≤ t ∧ ComesToBe (p a) t) : ¬ ∀ L : List α, ∃ t a, p a t ∧ ¬ a ∈ L
laws.says: Where what holds is listed at each step and coming to be does not recur, not unboundedly many members ever hold; strengthening to a covering list would give LPO.

laws.name: World.rest_needs_census; exposed_world; exposed_standing; openness_contingent; holding_world; hatch_rests_unrefuted; rest_needs_standing; exchange_needs
laws.statement: e.g. exposed_world : exposed.Premised ∧ exposed.ArisingRecurs ∧ ∀ t, ¬ exposed.flow.Enclosed t; holding_world : holding.Premised ∧ (∀ t, ¬ holding.flow.Enclosed t) ∧ ¬ holding.ArisingRecurs ∧ ¬ holding.CeasingRecurs ∧ ¬ holding.Finite

laws.name: Web.IncludesAlong, ExceedsAlong, WidensAlong
laws.statement: def IncludesAlong (e : F → F') (l : Nat → C → Nat) (l' : Nat → C' → Nat) : Prop := ∀ t f, W.Admits (l t) t f → W'.Admits (l' t) t (e f); def ExceedsAlong ... := ∃ t g, W'.Admits (l' t) t g ∧ ∀ f, e f = g → ¬ W.Admits (l t) t f; WidensAlong := IncludesAlong ∧ ExceedsAlong
laws.says: Comparison of what two level paths admit (levels meet every requirement's need), across two webs, along a map of formations. Admits uses only `requires` and `need`.

laws.name: Web.widensAlong_id_iff; IncludesAlong.comp; IncludesAlong.widensAlong_comp; WidensAlong.comp
laws.statement: widensAlong_id_iff : W.WidensAlong W id l l' ↔ W.Widens l' l
laws.says: Along the identity it is the package's Widens; inclusion composes; widening composes where the later step widens or the later map is one to one.

laws.name: Web.Growth, Web.grow, oldLevels
laws.statement: structure Growth (F N D C) where level : Nat → D → Nat; active : Nat → N → Prop; requires : Nat → N → C ⊕ D → Prop; need : Nat → N → C ⊕ D → Nat; draws : Nat → N → C ⊕ D → Prop; drawsNew : Nat → F → D → Prop. def grow (W : Web F C) (X : Growth F N D C) : Web (F ⊕ N) (C ⊕ D)
laws.says: A web with new formations and new conditions added. New formations may require and draw on old or new conditions; old formations may draw on new conditions; old formations' requirements are unchanged. No flow.

laws.name: Web.grow_admits_old; grow_includesAlong_iff
laws.statement: grow_admits_old : (W.grow X).Admits (l' t) t (.inl f) ↔ W.Admits (oldLevels l' t) t f
laws.says: An old formation is admitted in the grown web exactly where the old conditions' levels admit it.

laws.name: Web.grow_widensAlong_iff
laws.statement: W.WidensAlong (W.grow X) Sum.inl l l' ↔ W.Includes (oldLevels l') l ∧ (W.Exceeds (oldLevels l') l ∨ ∃ t n, (W.grow X).Admits (l' t) t (.inr n))
laws.says: For any level path l of the old web and l' of the grown web: l' widens l along the inclusion exactly where the old levels of l' admit every old formation l admits, and either admit more or some new formation is admitted at some step. The paths are arbitrary; nothing ties them to W.level, to X.level or to any taking.

laws.name: Web.grow_widensAlong_iff_new; grow_widens_unregistered
laws.statement: grow_widensAlong_iff_new (keep : ∀ t c, l' t (.inl c) = l t c) : W.WidensAlong (W.grow X) Sum.inl l l' ↔ ∃ t n, (W.grow X).Admits (l' t) t (.inr n); grow_widens_unregistered (keep) (added : ∃ t n, (W.grow X).Admits (l' t) t (.inr n)) : W.WidensAlong (W.grow X) Sum.inl l l' ∧ ¬ W.Widens (oldLevels l') l ∧ ¬ W.Widens l (oldLevels l')
laws.says: Assuming the old conditions' levels are exactly as they were, the grown world widens exactly where some new formation is admitted at some step, and on the old formations nothing widens or narrows. `keep` is a premise; no law says when it holds.

laws.name: Web.attach; attach_widensAlong_iff
laws.statement: def attach (p : F) (k : Nat) (level : Nat → Nat) : Growth F Unit Unit C (new formation requires only the new condition at need k, draws on it, active where k ≤ level t; drawsNew _ f _ := f = p). attach_widensAlong_iff (keep : ∀ t c, m t (.inl c) = l t c) : W.WidensAlong (W.grow (attach p k level)) Sum.inl l m ↔ ∃ t, k ≤ m t (.inr ())
laws.says: One new formation attached by one new condition, old levels kept: widening exactly where, at some step, the path's level of the new condition reaches k. The fields `level`, `active` and `drawsNew` of `attach` do not enter the statement (the level read is `m`, a free path).

beyond_the_guesses:
1. Two different "rests on" in Roles, never joined. A relatum is a condition of another through requiring (`active_of_bearing`, web only: requires at positive need plus Dependent) or through giving (`arises_given`, flow: Balances plus Acting). No law in Roles says that what requires an embodied relatum takes from it or is given to by it. The built examples keep them apart: in Brood generation t+1 is given by generation t but requires only itself; in Mutualism each requires the other and nothing is given or taken (no flow at all).

2. Embodiment is the hinge of every cost law, and it is a representational choice. Arising costs standing only where the arising thing is active exactly while its level is positive: `Flicker` arises for ever under balance and dissipation with nothing given. Embodied and SelfBearing change under relabelling of the condition side while Dependent and undermining do not (`Mutualism.apart_relabelled` :806, `Wilting.relabelled_not_embodied` :960). `EmbodiedSource` shows an embodied giver that takes, requires and draws on nothing.

3. On "does an arising make room for further arisings": the only general two-way statements about further arisings in my files are counting laws, and they say room comes from ceasing: with at most B active, arising recurs exactly when ceasing recurs (Openness.lean:366; for standing :157); with an unbounded count arising can recur with nothing ceasing (`slow_world` :524, `accretion`), but those worlds have levels 0 and a still flow. With levels and taking, under dissipation, every embodied arising lowers a closed family's stock and comes with another member's fall (Roles.lean:650, :672), and arising without end needs exchange beyond every enclosed family (:717; Openness.lean:676). Recurring arising with constant stock exists only as hand-off (Shuttle, Exposed, SprayShuttle: the same two sides alternate, each arising at the other's fall) or as giving from nothing (Brood).

4. Growth stands alone. By grep, `WidensAlong`, `IncludesAlong`, `ExceedsAlong`, `Web.grow`, `oldLevels`, `attach` are used in no other module. Its laws are about admission by level paths given from outside; `Growth.level`, `.active`, `.draws`, `.drawsNew` occur in no theorem. It has levels and needs, no flow, no taking, and no arising (`Arises` is not mentioned).

5. Novelty's "new" is a new list of levels of a fixed finite family of conditions, not a new formation. Its bearing on sense (c): a fixed family that is new at every step must have total level above every bound (`unbounded_of_new` :186); the law does not cover a family whose list of conditions grows.

6. Succession is one built example and nothing else. It is the nearest thing in my files to a going-on living on what another passes on with no needed level lowered (the eater takes each step the one unit that step's source gives the pool, the source having burnt two units of fuel nothing requires), but the eater does not arise, nothing requires anything, and the sources' activity is stipulated.

7. Where an opening account says more than the Lean, or names what is not in the file:
- Roles: its Results list presents `active_along`, `coextinct` and the fox's ending as results; they are in LabelledRoles.lean (the account's last paragraph says so). "A bee and a flower ... renew each other with no third condition" is, in Lean, a web with all levels 1 and all activity True by definition and no flow; `RenewingIn` holds because nothing changes. `Mutualism.apart_embodied` is in Correspondence.lean:621. The fox's ending also holds by the web's definition (both share the schedule `uneaten`).
- Novelty: the Readings sentence "novelty without end is gain without bound, which must come from beyond the part" has no counterpart in this module: `unbounded_of_new` concludes only that the stock exceeds every bound; no flow or beyond occurs in it.
- Openness: the account names `World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed` (InAmounts), `World.hatch_idle` and `World.counted_of_ever` (Premises), `Listed.ceasing_iff_shortfall` and `ceasing_of_outpacing` (Population), `World.lpo_of_finite_ends` (Counting), `Flow.change_recurs_iff` (Locality); none is in Openness.lean. The rest theorem's conclusion is `¬ ¬ ∃ N, RestsFrom N`, which the account does say.
- Succession: "what continuing needs is being fed, not any one feeder" is a reading of one built example; the eater continues by stipulation (`active` True) and requires nothing.
- Growth: account and Lean agree.

8. In all five files every "goes on" is stipulated in a built web; every general law concludes an ending, a lowering, a need for giving or exchange beyond, a count identity, or a fact about admission. This agrees with the first round's finding that on the web `active` is a free field.

2. The bounding quantity is not the inflow into the carriers' lineages taken together. SelectionPace.lean:329 `def carriedInflow (L : Flow X X) (G : Generations X) (t : Nat) : Nat := total (G.family t) fun p => G.amount t p * L.inflow (lineage [p] (G.kids t)) t`: summed parent by parent, weighted by the amount, over ALL parents, gifts between carrying lineages counted and not netted. `joint_within_carried` (:553) gives joint ≤ carried; in `Swap` carried is 2 and joint is 0. laws.name: Flow.DescendsAt, Flow.Descends
laws.statement: variable (L : Flow X X) (W : Web X X). def DescendsAt (t : Nat) (x g : X) : Prop := g ∈ L.present t ∧ 0 < L.give t g x ∧ W.ComesToStand t x. def Descends (x g : X) : Prop := ∃ t, L.DescendsAt W t x g. (Flow.lean:242: Web.ComesToStand W t c := ¬ 0 < W.level t c ∧ 0 < W.level (t + 1) c.)
laws.says: With formations and conditions of one type: x descends from g across the step from t when g takes part in the step, gives x something, and x's level rises from nothing. Balance is not part of it.

laws.name: SelectionPace.lineage, carriedInflow, carriers (with SelectionTerm.Generations)
laws.statement: def lineage (ps : List X) (kids : X → List X) : List X := ps ++ ps.flatMap kids. def carriedInflow (L : Flow X X) (G : Generations X) (t : Nat) : Nat := total (G.family t) fun p => G.amount t p * L.inflow (lineage [p] (G.kids t)) t. def carriers (G : Generations X) (t : Nat) : List X := (G.family t).filter fun p => nonzero (G.amount t p). structure Generations (α : Type) where first : List α; kids : Nat → α → List α; amount : Nat → α → Nat; family 0 = first, family (t+1) = (family t).flatMap (G.kids t); size t = (family t).length; sum t = total (family t) (amount t).
laws.says: A lineage here is a list: some parents followed by the relata listed as their offspring, for one step. Generations are a first list and a free assignment of offspring lists. The tie to the flow is only through the laws' premises (balance on the list, offspring coming to stand at m or more). DescendsAt is not used: no premise says a parent gives to its listed offspring.

laws.name: Flow.inflow
laws.statement: def inflow (L : Flow F C) (cs : List C) (t : Nat) : Nat := total (L.present t) fun f => excess (total cs (L.give t f)) (total cs (L.take t f))
laws.says: For a list of conditions and a step: summed over the formations taking part, what each gives the list beyond what it takes from it. A formation that takes more than it gives counts as nothing, not as a minus.

laws.name: Flow.gainlessOn_iff_inflow
laws.statement: theorem gainlessOn_iff_inflow : L.GainlessOn cs t ↔ L.inflow cs t = 0   (GainlessOn cs t := ∀ f, f ∈ L.present t → total cs (L.give t f) ≤ total cs (L.take t f), Entropy.lean:146)
laws.says: The inflow of a list at a step is zero exactly where every formation taking part gives the list no more than it takes from it. No premise.

laws.name: Flow.replenishment_le_inflow, Flow.gained_le_inflow
laws.statement: theorem replenishment_le_inflow (L : Flow F C) (cs : List C) (t : Nat) : L.replenishment cs t ≤ L.uptake cs t + L.inflow cs t. theorem gained_le_inflow (L : Flow F C) (cs : List C) (t : Nat) : excess (L.replenishment cs t) (L.uptake cs t) ≤ L.inflow cs t
laws.says: No premise. What a list is given across a step is at most what is taken from it with its inflow; what it is given beyond what is taken is at most its inflow.

laws.name: Flow.Balances.stock_gained, stock_inflow, stock_over_inflow, stock_lost
laws.statement: stock_gained (balances : L.Balances W) (cs) (t) : W.stock cs (t + 1) + L.lost cs t = W.stock cs t + excess (L.replenishment cs t) (L.uptake cs t). stock_inflow (balances : L.Balances W) (cs) (t) : W.stock cs (t + 1) + L.lost cs t ≤ W.stock cs t + L.inflow cs t. stock_over_inflow (balances : L.Balances W) (cs) : ∀ S N, W.stock cs (S + N) ≤ W.stock cs S + total (steps S N) (L.inflow cs). stock_lost (balances : L.Balances W) (gainless : L.GainlessOn cs t) : W.stock cs (t + 1) + L.lost cs t = W.stock cs t.  (lost cs t := excess (L.uptake cs t) (L.replenishment cs t), :562)
laws.says: In a balanced flow: a list's total level after a step with what it loses equals its total before with what it gains, and that is at most the total before with the inflow; over a stretch the total rises by at most the stretch's inflow; where the list gains nothing at a step its total falls by exactly what it loses. These are the only laws in Entropy.lean that mention inflow, besides the two entries above and GainlessOn.replenishment_le (:604).

laws.name: SelectionPace.born_within_inflow
laws.statement: theorem born_within_inflow {t m : Nat} {es ps : List X} {kids : X → List X} (balanced : L.BalancesOn W (es ++ ps.flatMap kids) t) (arise : ∀ p k, p ∈ ps → k ∈ kids p → W.ComesToStand t k) (stands : ∀ p k, p ∈ ps → k ∈ kids p → m ≤ W.level (t + 1) k) : m * born ps kids + total es (W.level (t + 1)) ≤ total es (W.level t) + L.inflow (es ++ ps.flatMap kids) t
laws.says: Take any list es and the offspring lists of any parents ps. If the flow balances at each member of es and each listed offspring across the step, and each listed offspring's level goes from nothing to m or more, then m for each offspring, with what es stands at after, is at most what es stood at before with the inflow into the whole list. es need not be the parents.

laws.name: SelectionPace.parent_within_inflow
laws.statement: theorem parent_within_inflow {t m : Nat} {p : X} {kids : X → List X} (balanced : L.BalancesOn W (lineage [p] kids) t) (arise : ∀ k, k ∈ kids p → W.ComesToStand t k) (stands : ∀ k, k ∈ kids p → m ≤ W.level (t + 1) k) : m * (kids p).length ≤ W.level t p + L.inflow (lineage [p] kids) t
laws.says: Under balance on a parent and its listed offspring at the step, each offspring coming to stand at m or more: the number of offspring times m is at most what the parent stood at with the inflow into the list of the parent and those offspring. This is the nearest general law to 'growth is within what lands on one's own lineage'; what the parent gives elsewhere does not enter.

laws.name: SelectionPace.generation_within_inflow
laws.statement: theorem generation_within_inflow {G : Generations X} {t m : Nat} (balanced : L.BalancesOn W (lineage (G.family t) (G.kids t)) t) (arise : ∀ p k, p ∈ G.family t → k ∈ G.kids t p → W.ComesToStand t k) (stands : ∀ p k, p ∈ G.family t → k ∈ G.kids t p → m ≤ W.level (t + 1) k) : m * G.size (t + 1) ≤ total (G.family t) (W.level t) + L.inflow (lineage (G.family t) (G.kids t)) t
laws.says: Same premises read on a whole generation: m times the next generation's size is at most what this generation stood at with the inflow into it and its offspring.

laws.name: SelectionPace.standing_pinned, stands_of_need
laws.statement: standing_pinned {G} {t m} (stands : ∀ p k, p ∈ G.family t → k ∈ G.kids t p → m ≤ W.level (t + 1) k) (capped : ∀ p, p ∈ G.family (t + 1) → W.level (t + 1) p ≤ m) : ∀ k, k ∈ G.family (t + 1) → W.level (t + 1) k = m. stands_of_need {s m : Nat} {k : X} (dependent : W.Dependent) (active : W.active s k) (requires : W.requires s k k) (need : m ≤ W.need s k k) : m ≤ W.level s k
laws.says: The two standing premises together fix every member of the next generation at exactly m. The second is the module's only use of active, requires and need: a relatum active at a step that requires its own standing at need m or more stands at m or more, where activity needs support.

laws.name: SelectionPace.offspring_within_carried, total_within_carried
laws.statement: offspring_within_carried {G} {t m} (balanced : L.BalancesOn W (lineage (G.family t) (G.kids t)) t) (arise : ∀ p k, p ∈ G.family t → k ∈ G.kids t p → W.ComesToStand t k) (stands : ∀ p k, p ∈ G.family t → k ∈ G.kids t p → m ≤ W.level (t + 1) k) (exact : Exact (G.family t) (G.kids t) (G.amount t) (G.amount (t + 1))) : m * G.sum (t + 1) ≤ total (G.family t) (fun p => G.amount t p * W.level t p) + carriedInflow L G t. total_within_carried: the same four premises and (capped : ∀ p, p ∈ G.family t → W.level t p ≤ m) : m * G.sum (t + 1) ≤ m * G.sum t + carriedInflow L G t.  (Exact ps kids a b := ∀ p, p ∈ ps → ∀ k, k ∈ kids p → b k = a p, SelectionTerm.lean:352)
laws.says: With each offspring carrying exactly its parent's amount: m times the next generation's total of the amount is at most the parents' standings weighted by their amounts with the carried inflow; and where each parent (carrier or not) stands at no more than m, at most m times this generation's total with the carried inflow.

laws.name: SelectionPace.response_within_carried
laws.statement: theorem response_within_carried {G : Generations X} {t m : Nat} (balanced : L.BalancesOn W (lineage (G.family t) (G.kids t)) t) (arise : ∀ p k, p ∈ G.family t → k ∈ G.kids t p → W.ComesToStand t k) (stands : ∀ p k, p ∈ G.family t → k ∈ G.kids t p → m ≤ W.level (t + 1) k) (exact : Exact (G.family t) (G.kids t) (G.amount t) (G.amount (t + 1))) (capped : ∀ p, p ∈ G.family t → W.level t p ≤ m) (sustained : G.size t ≤ G.size (t + 1)) : m * (G.size t * G.sum (t + 1)) ≤ m * (G.size (t + 1) * G.sum t) + G.size t * carriedInflow L G t
laws.says: The pace of a mean across one step. Six premises: balance on the generation and its listed offspring at the step; each offspring's level goes from nothing to m or more; each offspring carries its parent's amount exactly; every parent stands at no more than m; the next generation is no smaller. Then m times the cross-multiplied mean after is at most m times the cross-multiplied mean before with the size times the carried inflow.

laws.name: SelectionPace.selection_within_carried
laws.statement: Same six premises as response_within_carried (balanced, arise, stands, exact, capped, sustained) : m * G.concordAt t ≤ m * G.discordAt t + G.size t * carriedInflow L G t.  (concordAt t := concord (G.family t) (G.offspringNumber t) (G.amount t); concord ps w a := total ps fun p => total ps fun q => excess (w p) (w q) * excess (a p) (a q); discord with excess (a q) (a p), SelectionTerm.lean:193-198, 433-435)
laws.says: Under the same premises the selection term proper (how far more offspring go with more of the amount, over ordered pairs, against how far they go with less) is bounded: m times the concordance is at most m times the discordance with the size times the carried inflow.

laws.name: SelectionPace.unfed_rise_shrinks
laws.statement: (balanced) (arise) (stands) (exact) (capped) as in response_within_carried, and (positive : 0 < m) (unfed : carriedInflow L G t = 0) (rises : G.size (t + 1) * G.sum t < G.size t * G.sum (t + 1)) : G.size (t + 1) < G.size t
laws.says: With m positive and no carried inflow at the step, a rise of the mean leaves the next generation strictly smaller. One step; nothing is concluded over a stretch, and no ending is concluded.

laws.name: SelectionPace.inflow_lineage_le, joint_within_carried
laws.statement: inflow_lineage_le (kids : X → List X) (ps : List X) (t : Nat) : L.inflow (lineage ps kids) t ≤ total ps fun p => L.inflow (lineage [p] kids) t. joint_within_carried (G : Generations X) (t : Nat) : L.inflow (lineage (carriers G t) (G.kids t)) t ≤ carriedInflow L G t
laws.says: No premise. The inflow into several parents' lists taken together is at most the sum of the inflows into each parent's list; so the inflow into the carriers' joint list is at most the carried inflow. The carried inflow can be strictly more (Swap).

laws.name: SelectionPace.share_within_rest
laws.statement: theorem share_within_rest {G : Generations X} {t m : Nat} {rs : List X} (balanced : L.BalancesOn W ((carriers G t ++ rs) ++ (carriers G t).flatMap (G.kids t)) t) (arise : ∀ p k, p ∈ carriers G t → k ∈ G.kids t p → W.ComesToStand t k) (stands : ∀ p k, p ∈ carriers G t → k ∈ G.kids t p → m ≤ W.level (t + 1) k) (exact : Exact (G.family t) (G.kids t) (G.amount t) (G.amount (t + 1))) (capped : ∀ p, p ∈ carriers G t → W.level t p ≤ m) (unit : ∀ p, p ∈ G.family t → G.amount t p ≤ 1) : m * G.sum (t + 1) + total rs (W.level (t + 1)) ≤ m * G.sum t + total rs (W.level t) + L.inflow ((carriers G t ++ rs) ++ (carriers G t).flatMap (G.kids t)) t
laws.says: For an amount of zero or one, with the standing premises asked of the carriers only and any other list rs: m times the carriers' offspring count, with what rs stands at after, is at most m times the carriers' count with what rs stood at before and the inflow into carriers, rs and the carriers' offspring. By arithmetic on this statement (not a separate declaration): where that inflow is zero, rs falls by at least m for each unit the count rises. It bounds the total, not the mean, and nothing says the carriers require anything of rs.

laws.name: SelectionPace.share_within_joint
laws.statement: (balanced : L.BalancesOn W (lineage (carriers G t) (G.kids t)) t), arise, stands, capped of the carriers, exact, (unit : ∀ p, p ∈ G.family t → G.amount t p ≤ 1) : m * G.sum (t + 1) ≤ m * G.sum t + L.inflow (lineage (carriers G t) (G.kids t)) t
laws.says: share_within_rest with nothing else listed: for an amount of zero or one the total rises by at most the inflow into the carriers' joint list over m.

laws.name: SelectionPace.stretch_within_carried, moved_within_carried, steps_to_move
laws.statement: stretch_within_carried {G} {m} : ∀ T, (∀ t, t < T → balanced at t) → (∀ t p k, t < T → arise) → (∀ t p k, t < T → stands) → (∀ t, t < T → exact at t) → (∀ t p, t < T → p ∈ G.family t → W.level t p ≤ m) → m * G.sum T ≤ m * G.sum 0 + total (steps 0 T) (carriedInflow L G). moved_within_carried: the same five for all t < T and (sustained : G.size 0 ≤ G.size T) : m * (G.size 0 * G.sum T) ≤ m * (G.size T * G.sum 0) + G.size 0 * total (steps 0 T) (carriedInflow L G). steps_to_move: besides (bounded : ∀ t, t < T → carriedInflow L G t ≤ I) : m * (G.size 0 * G.sum T) ≤ m * (G.size T * G.sum 0) + G.size 0 * (T * I). (each 'balanced at t' etc. is the premise of total_within_carried at step t)
laws.says: Over T steps each meeting the step premises: m times the final total is at most m times the first with the carried inflow summed over the steps; where the final generation is no smaller than the first, the same for the cross-multiplied mean; with a cap I on each step's carried inflow, the bound is the first size times T times I. The inflow at each step is into that step's lists.

laws.name: SelectionPace.parent_within_factor, total_within_factor, total_within_power, share_within_power, whole_within_power
laws.statement: parent_within_factor {t m k} {p} {kids} (balanced : L.BalancesOn W (lineage [p] kids) t) (arise : ∀ c, c ∈ kids p → W.ComesToStand t c) (stands : ∀ c, c ∈ kids p → m ≤ W.level (t + 1) c) (capped : W.level t p ≤ m) (positive : 0 < m) (fed : L.inflow (lineage [p] kids) t + m ≤ k * m) : (kids p).length ≤ k. total_within_factor: balanced, arise, stands, exact, capped on the generation at t, positive, (fed : ∀ p, p ∈ G.family t → L.inflow (lineage [p] (G.kids t)) t + m ≤ k * m) : G.sum (t + 1) ≤ k * G.sum t. total_within_power (positive) : ∀ T, [the same for all t < T] → G.sum T ≤ k ^ T * G.sum 0. share_within_power: besides (sustained : G.size 0 ≤ G.size T) : G.size 0 * G.sum T ≤ k ^ T * (G.size T * G.sum 0). whole_within_power: besides (whole : G.size T ≤ G.sum T) : G.size 0 ≤ k ^ T * G.sum 0
laws.says: With m positive and a parent at no more than m: if the inflow into its own list with m is at most k times m, it leaves at most k offspring. Asked of every parent with exact transmission, the total multiplies by at most k a step and k to the T over T steps; with the population not shrinking the share does too; a final total reaching the final size needs the first size to be at most k to the T times the first total.

laws.name: SelectionPace.number_step_within_inflow, number_spread_within_inflow, number_unfed_uniform, response_sq_within_inflow
laws.statement: number_step_within_inflow (number : Reproduction.Generations.ByNumber G) (exact at t) (balanced : L.BalancesOn W (lineage (G.family (t + 1)) (G.kids (t + 1))) (t + 1)) (arise, stands at step t + 1) : m * (G.size (t + 1) * G.size (t + 1) + G.concordAt t) ≤ G.size t * (total (G.family (t + 1)) (W.level (t + 1)) + L.inflow (lineage (G.family (t + 1)) (G.kids (t + 1))) (t + 1)). number_spread_within_inflow: besides (capped : ∀ p, p ∈ G.family (t + 1) → W.level (t + 1) p ≤ m) (sustained : G.size t ≤ G.size (t + 1)) : m * G.concordAt t ≤ G.size t * L.inflow (lineage (G.family (t + 1)) (G.kids (t + 1))) (t + 1). number_unfed_uniform: besides (positive : 0 < m) (unfed : that inflow = 0) : ∀ p q, p ∈ G.family t → q ∈ G.family t → G.offspringNumber t p = G.offspringNumber t q. response_sq_within_inflow (exact at t) (inherited : ∀ p, p ∈ G.family t → ∀ k, k ∈ G.kids t p → G.offspringNumber (t + 1) k = G.offspringNumber t p) (balanced, arise, stands, capped at t + 1) (sustained) : m * ((G.size t * G.sum (t + 1) - G.size (t + 1) * G.sum t) * (same)) ≤ G.size t * L.inflow (lineage (G.family (t + 1)) (G.kids (t + 1))) (t + 1) * concord (G.family t) (G.amount t) (G.amount t) ∧ the same with the two products subtracted the other way.  (ByNumber G := ∀ t p, G.amount t p = G.offspringNumber t p, Reproduction.lean:371)
laws.says: Reading each member by its offspring number, carried over exactly: the spread of offspring numbers at a step (squared differences over pairs, times m) is at most the size times the inflow into the NEXT generation and its offspring at the NEXT step, where the next generation stands at no more than m and the population is not shrinking; with that inflow zero and m positive, all offspring numbers at the step are equal. Where offspring number is inherited besides an amount, m times the squared cross-multiplied change of the amount's mean is at most the size times that next-step inflow times the amount's spread.

laws.name: SelectionPace.Displacement.least, Fed.least
laws.statement: Displacement.least {Y} {L' : Flow Y Y} {W' : Web Y Y} {G : Generations Y} (balanced, arise, stands with m = 1, exact, capped at step 0) (sizes : G.size 0 = 2 ∧ G.size 1 = 2) (sums : G.sum 0 = 1 ∧ G.sum 1 = 2) : 1 ≤ carriedInflow L' G 0. Fed.least: ByNumber, exact at 0, balanced/arise/stands/capped at step 1 with m = 1, (sizes : G.size 0 = 2 ∧ G.size 1 = 2) (spread : G.concordAt 0 = 4) : 2 ≤ L'.inflow (lineage (G.family 1) (G.kids 1)) 1
laws.says: Over every world meeting the step premises with m one: these fixed counts need a carried inflow of at least one, and that spread needs an inflow of at least two. They are the response law and the spread law read at fixed numbers.

laws.name: SelectionPace.Displacement.natural_fails
laws.statement: theorem natural_fails : flow.inflow (lineage (generations.family 0) (generations.kids 0)) 0 = 0 ∧ ¬ (1 * (generations.size 0 * generations.sum 1) ≤ 1 * (generations.size 1 * generations.sum 0) + generations.size 0 * flow.inflow family 0) ∧ ¬ (1 * (generations.size 0 * generations.sum 1) ≤ 1 * (generations.size 1 * generations.sum 0) + generations.size 0 * flow.inflow (lineage (generations.family 0) (generations.kids 0)) 0) := ⟨rfl, by decide, by decide⟩
laws.says: One built example on five relata (pool, carrier, other, left, right), every level, take and give written out. At the first step the carrier takes one unit each from the pool, itself and the other member and gives one to each of its two listed offspring; all three fall to nothing, the offspring stand at one. The inflow into the members and offspring without the pool is nothing, and the response inequality with that inflow, or with the whole's inflow, in place of the carried inflow is false (4 ≤ 2). It refutes a candidate law; it is not a law. That the premises of the response law hold of it is `premises` (:1158); that the whole is closed, dissipated on and has no inflow, and that the law is met with equality at carried inflow one, is `displacement` (:1130).

laws.name: SelectionPace.Displacement.displacement, premises, rest_falls, factor, spread_needs_inheritance
laws.statement: displacement : flow.ClosedAt family 0 ∧ flow.DissipatesOn family 0 ∧ flow.inflow family 0 = 0 ∧ generations.size 0 = 2 ∧ generations.size 1 = 2 ∧ generations.sum 0 = 1 ∧ generations.sum 1 = 2 ∧ generations.concordAt 0 = 2 ∧ generations.discordAt 0 = 0 ∧ carriedInflow flow generations 0 = 1 ∧ [response law with =] ∧ [selection law with =]. rest_falls : carriers generations 0 = [carrier] ∧ total [pool, other] (web.level 0) = 2 ∧ total [pool, other] (web.level 1) = 0 ∧ [whole inflow = 0] ∧ [share_within_rest instance]. factor: sum doubles, k = 2 met. spread_needs_inheritance: concord of offspring numbers = 4, next-step inflow 0, every premise of number_spread_within_inflow but exact transmission of offspring number, and both next-step bounds false.
laws.says: The same five-relatum example read five ways: the bounds met with equality; the rest of the whole (pool and other member) falling from two to nothing while the carriers' count goes from one to two; the factor law met at two; and the spread bound failing where offspring number is not inherited. The web has active True, requires False, need 0.

laws.name: SelectionPace.Fed.fed, Inherited.same_step_fails, Inherited.next_step_attained, Inherited.stretch_attained, Swap.swap, Uncapped.uncapped, Shrink.shrink
laws.statement: Each a closed conjunction on its own inductive Relatum type with levels, takes and gives written out, proved by rfl, decide and instances of the general laws. Swap.swap : carriedInflow flow generations 0 = 2 ∧ carriers generations 0 = [left, right] ∧ flow.inflow (lineage (carriers generations 0) (generations.kids 0)) 0 = 0 ∧ sizes 2, 2 ∧ sums 2, 2. Uncapped.uncapped : carried inflow 0, every premise of response_within_carried with m one but capped, and the response inequality false. Shrink.shrink : carriedInflow flow generations 0 = 0 ∧ generations.size (0 + 1) < generations.size 0 ∧ ¬ [response inequality].
laws.says: Built examples: Fed meets the offspring-number bounds with equality; Inherited (two steps) shows the same-step form of the squared bound false and the next-step and stretch laws met with equality; Swap has two carriers each giving its unit to the other's listed offspring, carried inflow two against joint inflow nothing; Uncapped and Shrink show the response law false without a premise.

laws.name: Becoming.price (and selected_uniform)
laws.statement: theorem price (ps : List α) (kids : α → List α) (a b : α → Nat) : offspring ps kids b + lowered ps kids a b = selected ps kids a + raised ps kids a b. selected_uniform (ps) (kids) (a) (k : Nat) (same : ∀ p, (kids p).length = k) : selected ps kids a = k * total ps a
laws.says: An arithmetic identity with no premise and no flow: the offspring's total with what fell from parent to offspring equals the parents' amounts counted once per offspring with what rose. Where every parent has k offspring the weighted total is k times the parents' total, so it is not selection.

laws.name: Flow.DescendsAt.supported, Flow.unsupported_childless, Flow.never_supported_childless
laws.statement: DescendsAt.supported (acting : L.Acting W) (dependent : W.Dependent) {t} {x g} (descends : L.DescendsAt W t x g) : W.Supported t g. unsupported_childless (acting : L.Acting W) (dependent : W.Dependent) {t} {g} (unsupported : ¬ W.Supported t g) (x : X) : ¬ L.DescendsAt W t x g. never_supported_childless (acting) (dependent) {g} (never : ∀ t, ¬ W.Supported t g) (x : X) : ¬ L.Descends W x g.  (Acting: ∀ t f c, f ∈ L.present t → 0 < L.give t f c → W.active t f; Dependent: ∀ t f, W.active t f → W.Supported t f; Supported t f: ∀ c, W.requires t f c → W.need t f c ≤ W.level t c)
laws.says: Where only active formations give and a formation is active only where every condition it requires is at its need or more: a formation something descends from at a step is supported there; one unsupported at a step leaves no descendant across it; one never supported leaves none. One way, an ending of descent. No balance, no inflow, nothing about how many.

laws.name: Flow.selected_le, Flow.selection_within
laws.statement: selected_le (acting : L.Acting W) (dependent : W.Dependent) {t} {c} {ps} {kids} (descend : ∀ p k, p ∈ ps → k ∈ kids p → L.DescendsAt W t k p) (depends : ∀ p, p ∈ ps → W.requires t p c) : selected ps kids (fun p => W.need t p c) ≤ selected ps kids (fun _ => W.level t c). selection_within: the same and (b : X → Nat) : offspring ps kids b + lowered ps kids (fun p => W.need t p c) b ≤ selected ps kids (fun _ => W.level t c) + raised ps kids (fun p => W.need t p c) b
laws.says: Where every listed offspring descends from its parent at the step and every parent requires one condition c: the parents' needs of c, each counted once per offspring, are at most c's level counted once per offspring. It bounds a weighted total by a level, not a growth by an inflow; a parent with no offspring is not constrained.

laws.name: Flow.TransmitsWithin
laws.statement: def TransmitsWithin (L : Flow X X) (W : Web X X) (c : X) (δ : Nat) : Prop := ∀ t x g, L.DescendsAt W t x g → W.requires (t + 1) x c → W.requires t g c ∧ W.need (t + 1) x c ≤ W.need t g c + δ
laws.says: A premise, not derived: whatever descends and requires c after the step descends from something that required c, and needs at most δ more.

laws.name: Flow.transmitted_supported, Flow.transmitted_within
laws.statement: transmitted_supported (acting : L.Acting W) (dependent : W.Dependent) {c} {δ} (transmits : L.TransmitsWithin W c δ) {t} {x g} (descends : L.DescendsAt W t x g) (depends : W.requires (t + 1) x c) : W.need (t + 1) x c ≤ W.level t c + δ. transmitted_within (balances : L.Balances W) (acting) (dependent) {c} {δ} (transmits : L.TransmitsWithin W c δ) {S n} {x g} (descends : L.DescendsAt W (S + n) x g) (depends : W.requires (S + n + 1) x c) : W.need (S + n + 1) x c + total (steps S n) (L.uptake [c]) ≤ W.level S c + total (steps S n) (L.replenishment [c]) + δ
laws.says: A descendant's need of c is at most c's level at the step it was given, plus δ. In a balanced flow, that need with everything taken from c since an earlier step is at most c's level then with everything given to c since, plus δ. This is the one general law in Evolution that ties what a lineage can carry to what is taken from and given to a condition; it bounds a need, not a number of offspring.

laws.name: Flow.transmitted_along, Flow.transmitted_along_supported
laws.statement: transmitted_along {c} {δ} (transmits : L.TransmitsWithin W c δ) {xs : Nat → X} {ts : Nat → Nat} {n} (descends : ∀ i, i < n → L.DescendsAt W (ts i) (xs (i + 1)) (xs i)) (depends : ∀ i, i < n → W.requires (ts i + 1) (xs (i + 1)) c) (steady : ∀ i, i + 1 < n → W.need (ts (i + 1)) (xs (i + 1)) c ≤ W.need (ts i + 1) (xs (i + 1)) c) : ∀ i, i < n → W.need (ts i + 1) (xs (i + 1)) c ≤ W.need (ts 0) (xs 0) c + (i + 1) * δ. transmitted_along_supported: besides (founder : W.Supported (ts 0) (xs 0)) (pos : 0 < n) : … ≤ W.level (ts 0) c + (i + 1) * δ
laws.says: Here a lineage across generations is a sequence xs with xs (i+1) descending from xs i at step ts i. Along it, with each member requiring c and its need not rising until it gives, the need after i+1 descents is at most the founder's need plus (i+1) times δ; with the founder supported, at most c's level then plus that.

laws.name: Flow.goal_along, Flow.goal_descends_iff
